articles.title: Serbia has banished the monsters from Belgrade – it was, and still is, a truly wonderful revolution | Barbi Marković
articles.summary:
The Student List has shown my generation, who protested against the Milošević regime in the 1990s, how we should have done it

On Halloween, a few days after a student-led movement swept aside an illiberal, seemingly invincible regime in my native Serbia, I was sitting on the Vienna tram and watched various friendly and malicious monsters getting on and off around me. Witches, devils and unicorns were politely making their way to their respective parties.

Not all monsters wear fancy dress. Later that evening, I walked past a Serbian restaurant; in front of it stood a group of grumpy-looking men. They were smoking, spitting and swearing. I recognised the hardened, couldn’t-care-less attitude, the smell of corruption, the penchant for violence. Yet they looked as though their lives were coming to an end. These men are the losers of the revolution that is taking place in Serbia. Their smuggling routes and deals are under threat. Their criminal networks no longer function.

articles.title: Ukraine war briefing: Zelenskyy says Russia has damaged ‘every power plant’ as he seeks Latin American help
articles.summary:
Ukraine president tells leaders Kyiv needs equipment for its power grid – ‘and we need it fast’. Donald Trump predicts ‘very big’ deal with Russia. What we know on day 1,717

Volodymyr Zelenskyy has urged Latin American leaders to help Ukraine obtain urgently needed equipment to repair its power infrastructure damaged by Russian strikes. “Every power plant in Ukraine has been damaged in one way or another by attacks,” the Ukrainian president said at a summit in Madrid on Thursday, adding that repair crews were working around the clock. “We need as much international cooperation as possible to continue rebuilding and repairing our energy system,” he told a meeting on the sidelines of a summit of the Ibero-American Community, a 22-nation group of mainly Latin American Spanish- and Portuguese-speaking countries. “We know that companies in Spain and Latin America can help with this, can support this,” Zelenskyy said. “We need equipment that works with our power grid, and we need it fast.”

Donald Trump predicted a “very big” deal with Russia involving not only the Ukraine war but “all of Europe”, after meeting Russian president Vladimir Putin’s envoy. Trump revealed that he had an unscheduled meeting with Kirill Dmitriev, who was at the White House for talks with Ukrainian officials hosted by US first lady Melania Trump. “I can’t tell you what I discussed, but I’m just telling you, it’s going to be an agreement, it’s going to be a big agreement,” the US president told reporters in the Oval Office. “It’s going to be very big. It’s going to involve more than Ukraine, and I could even say it might involve all of Europe … everyone’s going to be thrilled.” Trump said he had not met with Ukrainian officials who were also at the White House on Thursday. His comments will fuel European concerns that he is pivoting towards the Kremlin and will pressure Ukraine towards an unfavourable deal to end Russia’s invasion.

Russia and Ukraine exchanged overnight airstrikes and one of Russia’s largest oil refineries appeared to have ⁠come under attack as a second day of talks on Ukraine’s postwar reconstruction and security guarantees wrapped up in Brussels on Thursday. A Ukrainian attack on a bus killed five people and wounded 13 in Ukraine’s Russian-occupied Luhansk region, according to its Moscow-backed leader, Leonid Pasechnik. In Komyshuvakha, near the frontline in Ukraine’s Zaporizhzhia region, rescue teams continued searching for more than 30 people believed trapped in the wreckage of a former school and a nearby shelter hit by Russian guided bombs on Monday. Zelenskyyy said 43 people had been confirmed dead, also saying one person previously reported missing had been found alive. In Russia, the Ryazan oil refinery appeared to have ⁠come under attack as part of a large overnight drone strike on industrial sites in the city south-east of Moscow, according to a Reuters video analysis.

Russia arranged to supply Iran with 90 launchers for advanced guided missiles, according to leaked defence industry documents that shed light on the depth of military cooperation between Moscow and Tehran. Pjotr Sauer reports that the documents, obtained by a Ukrainian private intelligence firm and shared with the Guardian, detail plans to supply Iran with launchers for the LMUR, a guided missile fired from attack helicopters which Russian forces have used extensively against Ukraine.

Italian prime minister Giorgia Meloni has slammed Europe’s “disorderly” approach to Ukraine negotiations and demanded the EU decide who speaks on its behalf, in a letter seen by Agence France-Presse. In the message to European Council chief António Costa, Meloni complained about the recent proliferation of meetings in different formats for talks on Russia’s war on Ukraine. “All this is making us look utterly lacking in credibility in handling one of the most complicated dossiers our nations are facing,” the Italian leader wrote. In response Costa wrote back that he agreed “Europe needs to act with coherence, unity and determination”.

archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech lze očekávat pokračující bezpečnostní dohled nad kritickou infrastrukturou v reakci na vlnu kybernetických útoků a napjatou politickou situaci v členských státech.
archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, continued security oversight of critical infrastructure can be expected in response to the wave of cyberattacks and tense political situations in member states.

archive.security_status_cs: Bezpečnostní situace v Evropě zůstává vysoce napjatá kvůli probíhající válce na Ukrajině, kde se diskutuje o nasazení západních mírových sil oprávněných opětovat palbu, a brutálním ruským útokům na civilní infrastrukturu. Vnitřní stabilitu členských států navíc narušují rozsáhlé občanské nepokoje, sociální protesty a eskalující politické spory ohledně právního státu v Polsku.
archive.security_status_en: The security situation in Europe remains highly tense due to the ongoing war in Ukraine, discussions over potential Western peacekeeping forces authorized to return fire, and brutal Russian attacks on civilian infrastructure. Furthermore, domestic stability in member states is being disrupted by widespread civil unrest, social protests, and escalating political disputes over the rule of law in Poland.
archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech lze očekávat zostřenou bezpečnostní ostrahu kvůli hrozícím kybernetickým útokům z Ruska a Číny a napětí spojenému s americkými volbami.
archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, heightened security vigilance can be expected due to looming cyber attacks from Russia and China and tensions linked to the US elections.

archive.security_status_cs: Evropa čelí zvýšenému napětí kvůli vlně kybernetických útoků na kritickou infrastrukturu napříč devíti státy a eskalaci konfliktu na Ukrajině po ničivých ruských úderech. Finanční trhy navíc vstřebávají blížící se výměnu v čele ECB a strukturální krizi evropského automobilového sektoru, zatímco politickou scénu zaměstnávají diskuse o britsko-evropském obchodu a geopolitické otřesy z Blízkého východu.
archive.security_status_en: Europe is facing heightened tensions due to a wave of cyber-attacks on critical infrastructure across nine states and the escalation of the conflict in Ukraine following devastating Russian strikes. Furthermore, financial markets are absorbing the impending leadership change at the ECB and the structural crisis in the European automotive sector, while the political scene deals with UK-EU trade talks and Middle Eastern geopolitical shocks.
archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech lze očekávat pokračující bezpečnostní ostražitost vůči kybernetickým hrozbám a intenzivní vyjednávání o nástupci Christine Lagardeové v čele ECB.
archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, continued security vigilance against cyber threats and intense negotiations over Christine Lagarde's successor at the ECB can be expected.

archive.security_status_cs: Evropa čelí stupňujícím se bezpečnostním a kybernetickým hrozbám, včetně útoků na francouzské krevní banky a eskalaci napětí na Blízkém východě s přímými hrozbami ze strany Iránu. Současně přetrvávají makroekonomické tlaky kvůli inflaci v Eurozóně a politická nestabilita v některých členských státech.
archive.security_status_en: Europe faces escalating security and cyber threats, including attacks on French blood banks and rising Middle Eastern tensions with direct threats from Iran. Simultaneously, macroeconomic pressures persist due to Eurozone inflation and political instability in several member states.
archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech lze očekávat další vyostřování geopolitické rétoriky, zvýšenou ostražitost kritické infrastruktury před kybernetickými útoky a pozorné sledování reakce ECB na inflační data.
archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, further escalation of geopolitical rhetoric, heightened vigilance of critical infrastructure against cyberattacks, and close monitoring of the ECB's reaction to inflation data can be expected.

archive.security_status_cs: Evropa čelí vlně vnitřních sociálních nepokojů, protestů a stávok v zemích jako Francie, zatímco přetrvávající inflační tlaky udržují Evropskou centrální banku v kurzu dalšího zpřísňování měnové politiky. Na geopolitické scéně eskalují dopady amerických politických zvratů na transatlantické vztahy a ukrajinský konflikt pokračuje s vysokou intenzitou ruských útoků na civilní infrastrukturu.
archive.security_status_en: Europe is facing a wave of domestic social unrest, protests, and strikes in countries like France, while persistent inflation pressures keep the European Central Bank on course for further monetary policy tightening. On the geopolitical front, the spillover effects of US political shifts on transatlantic relations are escalating, and the war in Ukraine continues with intense Russian strikes on civilian infrastructure.
archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech lze očekávat pokračující stávkovou vlnu a protesty v západní Evropě, zostřenou pozornost vůči kybernetické bezpečnosti kritické infrastruktury a napjaté vyjednávání o financování ukrajinské pomoci mimo rámec rozpočtu EU.
archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, further waves of strikes and protests in Western Europe, heightened focus on critical infrastructure cybersecurity, and tense negotiations over financing aid to Ukraine outside the EU budget framework can be expected.

archive.security_status_cs: Evropa čelí eskalujícím sociálním nepokojům, vlnám stávek v západních zemích kvůli životním nákladům a pokračujícím fatálním útokům na ukrajinskou energetickou infrastrukturu. Politickou scénu navíc komplikují mocenské boje v Německu před volbami a blížící se odchod prezidentky ECB Christine Lagardeové v únoru 2027.
archive.security_status_en: Europe is facing escalating social unrest, waves of strikes in Western countries driven by the cost of living, and ongoing fatal attacks on Ukrainian energy infrastructure. Furthermore, the political landscape is complicated by power struggles in Germany ahead of elections and the upcoming departure of ECB President Christine Lagarde in February 2027.
archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech lze očekávat pokračování masových protestů proti nákladům na život v západní Evropě a zostřený diplomatický tlak na dodávky energetického zařízení pro Ukrajinu. Na trzích bude přetrvávat nervozita spojená s vývojem v USA a měnovou politikou.
archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, mass protests against the cost of living in Western Europe and intensified diplomatic pressure for energy equipment supplies to Ukraine are expected to continue. Markets will remain nervous due to developments in the US and monetary policy.
